quest.title: Welkin Moon's Homecoming
quest.description: The moon has returned to its homeland. Under its silver glow, Nod-Krai will set forth toward a bright, new tomorrow...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act VIII
chapter.title: True Moon

talks.objective: Enjoy your morning in Nasha Town

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: ...No, you're doing it wrong. The moon looks like this now!

dialogues.speaker: Mahla
dialogues.text: Hmm? What are you drawing, children?

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: The new moon, Mom! It looks different than before, doesn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: Um, also — can I go buy a sugar sculpture today? Please? Just one!

dialogues.speaker: Mahla
dialogues.text: ...Alright. I suppose today is a special day, after all. Almost like a festival.

dialogues.speaker: Alida
dialogues.text: Extra, extra! Get the latest Nasha Express here!

dialogues.speaker: Alida
dialogues.text: "Post-Disaster Report! Nasha Town reborn beneath a new moon!"

dialogues.speaker: Alida
dialogues.text: "The voyage begins today! The future looks bright thanks to the League!" Want a copy?

dialogues.speaker: Arkhyp
dialogues.text: ...I knew things would be different, but I didn't think that would include the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: They say a new Moon Goddess has been born.

dialogues.speaker: Arkhyp
dialogues.text: A new moon goddess? Who's saying that? The Frostmoon Scions?

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: I guess so...? I'm not too clued up on the details. As far as I'm concerned, the moon's still in the sky, and it's business as usual.

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: Hey, since we've come all this way... Shall we grab ourselves a free meal while we're here?

dialogues.speaker: Arkhyp
dialogues.text: Are you a convert now? Or are you just here for the free lunch?

dialogues.speaker: Koski
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, what does it matter? After everything we've all just been through... Mmm, that smells good. Alright, that's it. I'm hungry. Time to eat.

dialogues.speaker: Vesa
dialogues.text: Come on! We gotta get there early, or there won't be any good spots left!

dialogues.speaker: Metta
dialogues.text: Shh, keep it down! This is the residential area. What if people are still sleeping?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, why is it so noisy outside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, Paimon was pretty much awake anyway. It's been so long since we last had a chance to relax, huh? Feels like time is moving slower than usual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about you? Did you rest well?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well enough. Somehow I wasn't as sleepy as much as I expected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still winding down from everything that's happened? Or are you wondering how our friends are doing? Or is it... about what Dottore said to you?

choices.text: A bit of everything, I think.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, if you say so. But don't push yourself, alright? Let Paimon know if you need to talk!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What we just went through was... a lot. It's totally normal if you need some time to get back in your groove.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Luonnotar disappeared after Columbina came back. Apparently, she was part of Columbina's soul or something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon kinda misses Luonnotar somehow...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But anyway, you did great, and so did Paimon. We all worked our butts off to contain this disaster, and in the end we made it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #So, chin up, {NICKNAME}. You should be proud of yourself!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're not usually this sharp when you've just woken up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Don't poke fun. You should be glad that Paimon's growing as a person!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sorry. On a more serious note...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I bet you were worried about me again, weren't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon didn't think you'd mention it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm sorry, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sob*... You... You have no idea how anxious Paimon was. She was worried sick about you...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you really wanna show Paimon you're sorry, you're gonna need to make it up to her... You'd better be ready to splash out on a lavish meal!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anything for you. My treat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew! Okay. Paimon's full now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you sure? Snacks will be served shortly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Ooh, well... Hmm...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: #Hey there, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Good morning!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Morning, Jahoda! Here for some breakfast?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Oh, I've already eaten, just need some water. I was mostly worried you might forget what day it was today, so I came over to remind you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...*burp*

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Careful there, Paimon. Too much food will make you drowsy. Don't let anyone catch you hiding at the back and nodding off during the League meeting...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You should probably be saying that to Aino. She's the baby of the group, if anyone.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: True... You know, I'm surprised that all these competing groups are actually coming together to try and solve things together. Definitely a first for Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, nothing like a region-wide calamity to bring people together... After that, surely even the most self-interested people have to realize that going it alone isn't worth the risk, right?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Heh, try telling Boss Nef that. She's not exactly convinced that people are gonna get with the program.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? But if she's so pessimistic about it, why'd she agree to be the Curatorium's representative in the league?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Probably 'cause... even though unity sounds like a pretty far-fetched idea, the benefits it would bring make it worth a shot.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: I think things'll work out, though. I swear Nod-Krai feels like one big family now, with everything that's happened. More than it used to, anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's with you on that one. And it seems like plenty of other people agree, too — just listen to the bustling streets!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Right? Everyone's been busy rebuilding these last two weeks, and the evacuees have been coming back in droves.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Life's slowly returning back to normal... *sigh* Which means, my workload's probably gonna shoot back up...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Were you about to head out? There's still some time before the ceremony begins, you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we were gonna take a stroll around the square and say hi to some friends first.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Sounds good. Seeya later then!

choices.text: But don't worry. I'm feeling okay.
Sure you don't need five more minutes?

talks.objective: Go to the central plaza in Nasha Town

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Please accept today's boon. Have a nice day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are Paimon's eyes deceiving her, or... is that Ineffa handing out food for the Frostmoon Scions?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Hello there. Would you like a Feast of the Moon, along with some snacks of the day?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, uh, what's new, Ineffa? It was only a few days ago when we last saw you, but... it looks like you've joined the Frostmoon Scions in that time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Aino, too!?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: What are you talking about, Paimon? We're just here to help, duh!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: In the wake of the disaster, it's all hands on deck. We responded to Lauma's request for support.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: "At times like these, the smallest good deed can inspire others and help them through the hard days ahead."

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: And we're using eggs and heating tubes to make that a reality, in true Krumkake Craftshop style!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Great work, Aino.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: #Ineffa, Ineffa! Did you hear that? {NICKNAME} said I did good! {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: That's because it's true, Aino. Proposal: If you can resist eating today's dessert, I will provide you with compliments, too.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: No way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that proposal got shot down quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hmph. I need something to get me through the hard times too, y'know!

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: ...Mom!

dialogues.speaker: Mahla
dialogues.text: Yes, dear. Go right ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ahem...

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: E—Excuse me! Could I... Could I take a photo with the robot lady?

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: She helped us get safely out of Nod-Krai, and she helped us get back home, too. She's the best!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hehe, of course she is! Aaand, since I'm the whiz kid who built her, that makes me even better than best, right?

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: Uhh... But you stole my snacks, though...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Oops...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Shall we move to the open space near the center? The view there is better.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll take the picture.

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: You look so cool when you fly, Miss Robot. And when you use your spear, too!

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: And... even though you took my snacks, it's pretty cool that you could build stuff like this. You've got so many inventions, it's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: Also... Also...

dialogues.speaker: Mahla
dialogues.text: Maika, we need to go now.

dialogues.speaker: Maika
dialogues.text: One second!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Please take this Feast of the Moon, as well as some snacks.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Share them with your mother and your lovely family.

talks.objective: Go to the central plaza in Nasha Town

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...Aren't you the better pick for this job, Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You underestimate yourself yet again, Master Illuga.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Not at all! I rarely come by Nasha Town. I don't know any of the big shots here.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: All in good time. Socializing is a step-by-step journey.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: But you're much further ahead on that road, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You're not seeing the full picture. You know the truth now. My friends do not understand my habits.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: There is no question about it. The Lightkeepers need a representative in the League. Someone who is upright, cares about other people, and can realize their self-worth through group action.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: You say it like you wouldn't make the cut.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I am most flattered that you think I would.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Sigh a little less, Master Illuga, and have more faith in yourself. All the Lightkeepers agree that you're a very promising young man.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That is precisely why Starshyna Nikita felt safe delegating such important work to you.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'm sure we all also agree that we would sooner die of dehydration than manage to wrangle anything out of you in a discussion.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hah... My apologies. I am not in the habit of bringing water with me when I go out.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Whatever. I'll take the job. By the way, who else is part of this?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh, it's quite the who's who of Nod-Krai. There's the Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, the Boss of the Curatorium of Secrets, a representative of the Voynich Guild, and even someone from the adorable Krumkake Craftshop...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I'm sure you will find speaking with them to be a genuine pleasure.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: If you say so. I've never done this work before, so I'm honestly a little scared of making mistakes...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: But I'll do it. Not only is it our duty as Lightkeepers, but... because I want to make Nod-Krai a more welcoming place.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: An admirable attitude to take. The beacons are lit, Illuga. We're but one step away from breaking through the blizzard.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: We have the chance to band together and build our shared homeland into an Elysium... This is unprecedented for Nod-Krai. An opportunity not to be missed.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Yeah... You're right. I'll do my best.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Quite a few familiar faces have arrived. Let's go, shall we?

talks.objective: Go to the central plaza in Nasha Town

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, everyone's here!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You seem well-rested.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I know no one's asked, but I'm sure you all wanna know. So let me just say: We're doing great, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well... great, but not perfect. I'm starting to lose my mind from boredom... Can't drink a drop of alcohol while I'm waiting for my wounds to heal.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'm sure you had a sneaky swig or two...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Wait, how'd you find out!?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Heh. I'm sure you must be missing Mondstadt after all these years away, Grand Master.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah, you can say that again. Every time I get news from Mondstadt, it makes me want to go back and see the place for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Honestly, once things are wrapped up here, I think it'll be time to head back home.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hey. Looks like someone's taking the stage.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Can everyone see okay? Anyone need a boost?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Uh... I'll just listen from the back, it's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're taking this pretty seriously, huh, Durin?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Well, it's not everyday I get the chance to see how people speak in official settings.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Soak it up like a sponge. I'll make sure you get a chance to practice for yourself later down the line... Actually, I know just the thing! You can debrief the Knights of Favonius for me.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Mr. Varka, are you forgetting that I'm not a Knight of Favonius...?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Eh, I can knight you. Any particular title you'd like?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Is he joking? I really can't tell.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You'll have to figure this one out for yourself. It'll be a good learning experience.

dialogues.speaker: Tarno
dialogues.text: It is my honor to host the opening ceremony for the League, and to have this opportunity to speak to you all in my capacity as Voynich Guild representative.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: (Could this person also have been pushed onto the big stage by the real big shots? Guess I'm not the only one, then...)

dialogues.speaker: Tarno
dialogues.text: ...We come here today having weathered the trials and hardships of yesterday, and having learned from them the importance of unity and cooperation.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Alright, here we go! ...Uh-oh, looks like Aino's off in dreamland already. Wait, Boss is looking kinda drowsy too... What's up with her?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...Come on, get this speech over with already...)

dialogues.speaker: Tarno
dialogues.text: ...Nod-Krai is our home, the land we rely on for survival. And as we chart a course for the future, may we persevere through the storms ahead as we sail towards a new era of prosperity, freedom, and hope...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Looks like we'll have more opportunities to travel in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm sure you'll cope, Lady Moonchanter, given how fleet of foot you are.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, I suspect I'll be too busy at the Curatorium to act as your host. We have a busy schedule, not to mention an international network of contacts to manage.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It'll be alright. I'll just check your schedule with Jahoda well in advance. And if she's not available, I can simply ask Ashru.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You... Ugh, so giving my employees extra workload isn't enough for you? You're really going to drag my cat into this, too?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I thought you'd approve. Aren't you forever increasing your employees' workloads?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmph, that's a bold statement... Are all the Frostmoon Scions feeling more audacious now that your Moon Goddess has returned?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Columbina's return has brought joy to all who care about her. That includes both you and me.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As for the Frostmoon Scions, we are learning how to thrive independently, without relying on the Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It is up to us to make our home a more livable place. Joining the League is one of the steps we are trying towards that end.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I like the word "try." It's nice and non-committal. You can opt out at any time and still say you tried.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hmm? You don't see a bright future for the Frostmoon Scions? Or did you mean the League?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm just not as optimistic as you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Frostmoon Scions should count themselves lucky that they have a leader as stubborn and enterprising as you...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But Nod-Krai's a big place with all kinds of people. Most of them don't enjoy answering to a leader, or even listening to reason.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, that's where you and your methods come in.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Unless... the Curatorium of Secrets is only here for appearances?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: For now, yes. And that won't change until this venture becomes worth my while.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What would make it worth your while?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Getting out more than I put in. Right now, I'd barely break even. But I'll grant that it's a good start for Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Then maybe it's worth a try.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Alright, you can stop now. Or do I have to join the Frostmoon Scions before you'll get off my back?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hmm... You'd be very welcome to join us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! That was a tight squeeze...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you two. Congrats on all your hard work! What are you chatting about?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Nefer was trying to dissuade me from adding to her employees' workload. Also, she's considering joining the Frostmoon Scions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Sorry, what?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hehehe, your conversations are always the most interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Would you two care to join me for some tea before heading to your next destination?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nicole? ...Wait, where are you? Aren't you gonna show up today?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Sadly not — I'm otherwise occupied right now. I'm sorry Paimon. I can hear how disappointed you are.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: If it's any consolation, let me say that how things appear on the surface is a far cry from what they are at their core...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Perhaps you'll feel better if you focus on the fact you have a special line of communication with the great mage herself...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: ...Assuming I still count as a Mage... which I suppose I probably do. I think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, okaaay...? Has something happened?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: No. Or, not yet, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well that's not ominous at all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there something we should be watching out for...?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Not for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Just think of this as a general check-in to make sure this communication system is still running smoothly. Besides, it's good to chat once in a while if we want to maintain our friendship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, you could've just said so. Paimon got all worked up for nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, the best friendships are built through face-to-face interaction, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's never gonna stop being weird having tea with you when you're not there, and just... talking to thin air.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alright, fair point. I'll bear that in mind for next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mind if I ask what's keeping you occupied?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, any update on that crisis at the world's borders?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alice just informed me that they had their work cut out for them, and now everyone's thoroughly exhausted, but they did finally get things back under control. Still, we can't let our guard down yet.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The disruption caused by this disaster has made Teyvat easier to detect from the outside universe.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: She plans to wait for things to stabilize, then reschedule her Mondstadt vacation plans.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: As for me, I agree with Hat Guy's perspective. This is a time when many new variables are emerging and the situation is changing constantly... plus, most of this change is for the worse.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: We have to remain vigilant and ensure that the embers of chaos are not rekindled.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I did notice that the energy in Nod-Krai changed somewhat after the war of funerary flame, but since it was still aligned with the Light Realm, I never gave it a second thought.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: *sigh* It looks like I'll have to examine the connections between phenomena I observe more closely in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like you've got a lot on your plate.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Just doing my duty. It's more or less second nature by now.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Of course, to give you the full picture, I'd have to start with the substance from which Angels were formed...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Heh, never mind. Paimon's right — showing off my knowledge would be much more satisfying in person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: By the way, you did receive the gifts from the Hexenzirkel, yes? I'm not trying to claim credit or anything, but my pride demands that I at least mention it...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: They're quite similar to the protective talisman that Alice gave Dori, but with some very special enhancements!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh! So that's what kept our friends safe when Dottore trapped them?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Indeed. We went to great lengths to make sure they were invisible to his eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ahaha... I'm so happy they came in handy... Still not fishing for gratitude, by the way. I just want you to be aware that sometimes, your friends may be protecting you in ways you cannot perceive.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'll contact you if anything else crops up. If not, you know what they say — no news is good news.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: ...Oh, my angelic instincts are tingling! They say...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You should head to the docks next... your friends are about to board their ship home!

talks.objective: Head to the port and look for your companions

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're here too, Hat Guy? Are you heading back together?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No. I'm bound for Sumeru, and she for Fontaine. We just happened to cross paths at the harbor.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Everything seems fine. Sandrone may have an abominable temper, but she's always been very responsible with important calculations, and things entrusted to her by valued friends.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: You always speak as if you know us inside out, Mr. Hat Guy.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...Maybe I'm just a good judge of character?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I certainly hope that's all there is to it.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Regardless, you have been a significant help in this matter. For that, you have my gratitude.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Eh... I didn't do anything special...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Sandrone's the one who completed a seemingly impossible formula and turned the tide of the entire battle... even giving her life in the process. She's the one we should be thanking.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: ...Even we were unaware that Sandrone had hidden the real formula inside Pulonia's body.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: She managed to fool Dottore into thinking the formula was running in her system, by installing a identical-looking decoy within her...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: She probably realized that she didn't have the strength to stop Dottore... but this way, she could at least get him to lower his guard.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Heh... She always worked like that. Always had a backup plan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What will happen to her body?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Well... that's why I'm traveling to Fontaine. She made a request of me long ago, and the time has come to fulfill it. Think of it as her will.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was the request?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: She said that, should she ever fail in a mission, she'd like me to deliver her core and Pulonia's to the Fontaine Research Institute.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: She also mentioned that she had made arrangements for people there to set her affairs in order.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Some of her personal effects, such as her notes, were left to me. I've decided to take them back to the House of the Hearth — for safekeeping, primarily, but also... as mementos, I suppose.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: However, there is one book among them that I'd like to leave in your care. I'll have someone deliver it to your residence at The Flagship at a later date.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Does Columbina know about this?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: No. I was specifically warned not to tell her.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: This is her last wish, and I will abide by it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Is it also some kind of "backup plan"?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I can only hope so... But none of us here can know for certain.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I bade farewell to Columbina earlier today. As promised, she turned the Iridescent Moon's marrow over to me.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: She... spent a long time with Sandrone's body, saying her goodbyes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Is she alright?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Sandrone's passing has left a great wound in all of our hearts. It will take time to heal.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: But Columbina surprised me — she offered me some words of comfort before I departed. Despite being grief-stricken herself, she showed an awareness of the feelings of others around her.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: ...She never used to act like this. Clearly, she has grown. And I suspect that we have you to thank for much of the change we are seeing in her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was a group effort by all of her friends.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Heh... After these recent events, the Tsaritsa has revoked the Palestar Edict.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Snezhnaya now realizes that the arrest warrant for Columbina was just a ploy by Dottore, who coveted her powers.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: ...I shall return to Nod-Krai to see her as soon as I find the time. I hope that from now on, she too will explore more of the world.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Columbina Hyposelenia's journey is only beginning.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: ...My ship is here.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we shall meet again. You too, Hat Guy.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: What are you still bumming around for? Isn't Columbina waiting for you?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I thought today was the day you'd agreed with her to go find out the truth about your sibling.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm a little nervous...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: You're afraid you won't like the truth when you see it?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hah... Well, this is new. I was starting to think that nothing could scare you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't say that. Wouldn't you be if you were in this situation?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: #Fair point. But I'd say I have more experience facing up to unpleasant truths than {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: They say blood's thicker than water. I know how much you need your family back — more than you need any of your friends. And I'm sure that all your real friends understand that, too.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: No matter what the truth turns out to be, they will stick by you and support you, whatever decision you make.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Finding the truth is important. But more important still is what you choose to do once you've found it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #{REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: At least, that's the life lesson I've learned from my experience grappling with the truth.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you feel better now than you used to?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: What, now that Dottore's dead and gone? A little, I guess. But it hasn't solved everything.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Maybe I regret not getting to end his life with my own hands, or maybe it's something else. But for whatever reason, I still feel like I have a chip on my shoulder.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Either way, I'm going back to Sumeru. Lesser Lord Kusanali is gonna need help dealing with all the chaos Dottore left in his wake. Not just from this incident, but everything he did in the past, too.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: You should continue with your journey, as you've always done. Who knows? Maybe we'll meet again someplace else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what should we do now? If you wanna explore a bit more to steady those nerves, Paimon's game.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, when Columbina said she knew where your ship was hidden, Paimon promised to give you two some alone time with the "truth."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It hasn't been all that long since we were last apart, sure... but with Columbina there, Paimon's sure things'll be just dandy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, ain't no biggie. Paimon might be all about that food and fun, but she knows how to do right by people!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon's sure you'd prefer to digest the news about your {M#sister}{F#brother} in peace.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But uh, no matter what you see... Just know you can share it with Paimon — 'course, as long as it's not super private!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you can't make sense of something, let's give it some thought together. And even if we both can't figure it out, Paimon can at least treat you to a nice meal!

choices.text: Who am I to refuse you, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, glad to hear it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feel better now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty! Next up, time to meet with Columbina!

choices.text: You're my best companion, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Columbina! We're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can't quite believe we're meeting out here. We'd gotten used to walking over to Silvermoon Hall whenever we'd go see you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hehe. Well, you're still welcome to go there whenever you want to see me.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's just, now that it's all over, I've decided to make some changes... Try and fit in with the Frostmoon Scions, like Lauma suggested.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And how's that been going?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Umm... The older generation are still timid around me. They don't dare to get too close, and they bow their heads when I walk by.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But things are much better with the children. I see more curiosity in their eyes.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hopefully, by the time the next Moon-Prayer Night comes around, I can enjoy the festival with them as myself, without having to pretend that I'm only dressed up as the Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You'll do fine, Columbina! Paimon's sure they'll realize you're super nice once they get to know you better.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You really think so? When we first met, you thought I was a little "up in the clouds"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—We were just starting out then, c'mon! Ugh, so Lauma told you, huh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hehe, I'm only teasing. I know that I have you to thank for pulling me back down to solid ground.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It feels good to finally stand firm on the earth where I was born.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, that's great!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well, then... are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #({M#Lumine}{F#Aether}... What happened to our spaceship back then? Why did you leave?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's time to learn the truth at last.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready as I'll ever be.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Good. Then let me open the way for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where does this lead?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: To our shared destination.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you remember me telling you about my missing prologue back when we'd just met? I said that my story began on the moon.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But while I was inside the moon's reflection, I realized that my prologue was really hidden in the future. I just had yet to discover it at that point.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The story of the time before I was born was in fact the story of my distant future... It's truly fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But when I obtained the trilunar authority and returned to our present reality, I sensed something I hadn't expected: your prologue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you mean...!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. Your spaceship. All this time, it has been hidden on the Frost Moon, which lay beyond the sky.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The "great ruler of the firmament"... the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, them!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why would they do that...?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I don't know. Perhaps your ship contains something that is incompatible with Teyvat. Or something that cannot be known.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Oh... Did I pick a bad time to say this? I know it must have been hard to work up the courage to do this.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Maybe I should have waited until you were on the moon, with no chance to back out...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, that would've been kinda mean, y'know...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Take me there.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Oh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Whatever is hiding in that ship... It belongs to me and {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}. Those memories belong to us.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No one else has the right to decide whether I should or shouldn't know about it. Not even the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Very well. Then let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Y—You two take care, alright? And don't forget to come back soon!

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: #Rest assured, Paimon, we will. {NICKNAME}, after you.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Thinking about the story that we'll find hidden on the moon?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Yes... and hoping that it has a happy ending.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Stories like that don't exist, you know.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...You don't believe in happy endings?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I don't believe in endings.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, you can have this back now.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Thank you. I'll make sure not to lose it this time.

choices.text: But why? Who could have done this...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I'll stay here with Columbina for a little longer...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Should we return to Teyvat now?)

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We'll be staying in Nod-Krai for a while longer to wrap some things up for Grand Master Varka.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Sure, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Do you miss home?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Um... To be honest, I do. I know the Grand Master's been away from Mondstadt for much longer, but for me... this is the longest I've been away from home in my life.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If there's anything you'd like to say to your friends back home, I'm sure Varka would be happy to write it down in a letter for you.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Ah, there's no need. I prefer talking face to face. Seeing their expressions and reactions makes me feel at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Our spaceship...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's huge... I suppose that the moon is the only place one could hide it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #It'll be alright, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The way you feel in this moment, I went through it too, on Moon-Prayer Night. The door was right in front of me, but I struggled to find the courage to step through.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Solitude for me once meant living a life in which even I was absent. Before I met you, that was the only life I knew.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But that night, solitude meant throwing away the life I had gained after meeting all of you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Go. Retrieve the part of your life that once was lost. Trust me, you will lose nothing by doing so.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Look. Teyvat is right there. All our friends are down there waiting for us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...You're right. Thanks, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? Finished?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Why did you take your eye mask off?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well... Since my return, I've decided to take more opportunities to see the world with my own eyes.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Besides... I've always wondered how Teyvat looks from the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And what do you think?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's beautiful. I could spend a whole day here just gazing at it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What about you? What do you think of the truth you found?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I haven't looked at another person's expression in a long time, but... I think yours is saying... it was neither good nor bad?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Heh. Keep this up, and it won't be long before you give Nefer a run for her money.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh... I don't think that's going to happen. I'm much more used to sensing what's going on around me with kuuvahki. I think I'll save my eyes for seeing special moments I really want to remember.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I... read the spaceship's flight logs.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I always assumed that this was my first time in Teyvat... I thought that {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} and I must have been hibernating in space for centuries on end...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But the logs show that our spaceship flew over the skies of Teyvat once before. A long, long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Flew over? So you didn't you land?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No. The ship barely came to a stop before flying on again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: After that, it continued traveling through space for a long time. Some of the data is corrupted, but I suspect that it kept flying for thousands of years.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was only after that that the ship made a forced landing in Nod-Krai...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(When {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} found me, {M#she}{F#he} came from outside the ship...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Could this mean that {M#she}{F#he} left the ship long before I did? Maybe even... during our first pass over Teyvat?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes... I can feel that the truth is coming together, one small piece at a time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I remember {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} telling me that when {M#she}{F#he} first arrived in Khaenri'ah, {M#she}{F#he} could not recall the past...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #So this might be something that even {M#she}{F#he} doesn't know...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Here, I made some space for you. Your mind must be racing, and this seems like the perfect place to relax and clear your head.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh! ...Wait, there's one more thing!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait here a moment...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Hey, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm...? Is that... a new outfit?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An old one, technically. It's been in a cabinet inside the ship this whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #It's a matching pair with {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}'s. {M#She}{F#He} always liked this set more...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Huh. I don't think there's a huge difference.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. It's still the same you. You're the same person, no matter what clothes you wear.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Haha... Only Columbina would make an observation like that...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}, do you consider Teyvat your home?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Home is... wherever {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} is. But then, after all the time I've spent here, and everything I've been through...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Yes, I'd say it's my home.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Would you change your answer if Teyvat changed appearance? I mean... if the truth about Teyvat turned out to be different than what you thought.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...I don't know. But I don't think so.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The truth is not what matters most to me about Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: When I was first born, I longed for a home...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And when you get something before you're mature enough to understand the world, you just take it at face value.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I thought that a home was a transaction. You give me what I want, and I'll do the same for you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But you and your friends taught me what a true home should look like. You never asked for anything, yet you gave so generously to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's because your friendship matters to us. It was worth it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Haha... In the past, I thought that my birth in Nod-Krai must have been a mistake.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But after journeying to the distant past where the story began, I realized that it was I who chose Nod-Krai to be my future home.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Now, I am glad that I made that choice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sure your friends are just as glad.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: In fact, I intend to make the same choice today as I did back then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well, I've given the Eternal Moon's marrow to Lauma, and the Iridescent Moon's Marrow to Arlecchino.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And now, I shall return my kuuvahki to Nod-Krai again, that it may continue to protect my chosen home.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait! But what about your body...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? ...Oh, are you worried that I'll disappear again?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Haha... I won't, not this time. The Frost Moon has now entered the false sky, and I am the Trilune Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I am only returning to Nod-Krai the part of me that it needs. I am giving what I can... because my home is worth it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, and I have something for you too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: For me?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. Come closer...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What was that?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I lifted some of the restrictions this world placed on you. I trust this will help in your future adventures?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (My power... It feels like it's grown. I can use the elements more freely now...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Thank you. This will be a great help.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You're welcome. I see you as family, and after everything you've done for me, I... In fact, no. It's not because I owe you. It's because you're worth it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Here. This flower is for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm? Isn't this a Moon-Prayer Blossom?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. Don't worry, you will never see these flowers lose their color again.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'm finally discovering the joy of giving... How I wish I'd learned this sooner.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey, better late than never.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you thinking about now?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Why don't you take a guess? You get... one shot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think I'll get it in one guess. But I'm sure it's a happy thought...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That's kind of a sneaky answer... I can't say you got it wrong.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Down in Teyvat, the moon seems so far away. I felt it might always lie beyond my reach...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But on the moon, everything feels so close by.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The haze that once enshrouded the skies has finally been dispersed. I feel like a traveler on a winter's night, starting a new chapter in my tale by the warmth of a bonfire.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I don't have a lot of luggage, but I do have a lot of hope for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Haha... Well, what's next?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Next?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: To start with... I want to stay here just a little longer.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: After that, let's return home and continue our journey.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: We're here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Over there.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The journey goes on, for you and for me.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Like I said, this is not the end. I don't believe there has to be an ending.

choices.text: Could you tell me a little bit about Snezhnaya?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Oh, is that your next destination?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Hmm... Most people would probably tell you to pack some warm clothes. But I experience things differently than most people, so I can't I know how cold it is.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: In fact, it is home to quite a wondrous heat source... I think they call it "Kresnik's Torch." Every city in Snezhnaya is built around one of those.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I sensed the energy it gave off as I was passing by on a railway train. It felt... grand, and distant.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I also recommend the Korolevskiy Troupe in Snezhnograd. They give performances quite regularly, and entry was free for Harbingers... I liked them a lot.

choices.text: What do you know about the Tsaritsa?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Hmmm. Ice-cold... and sharp. Crystal clear in some ways, yet profoundly unfathomable in others. Like the thick layer of ice on top of a frozen lake...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Hmm? That's just the impression the Tsaritsa gives me. I was never able to glimpse what truly lies beneath that icy exterior.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: In fact, I don't think the people of Snezhnaya even know what kind of power their god wields.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Maybe that's because the Tsaritsa herself has never acknowledged, nor accepted that power...

choices.text: Tell me more about the Fatui.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: There's Regrator, The Rooster... and The Jester.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Between them, they control a lot of what happens in Snezhnaya. But I could never wrap my head around how exactly power is split between them. I just know they are each responsible for many specific domains.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I noticed that The Rooster and Regrator often appeared to get along on the surface, while working against each other in secret... And theirs is not a friendly rivalry.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But I wasn't particularly interested, so I tended to keep my distance. Now that I think about it, the term "Mistilteinn" often seemed to come up in connection with Project Stuzha...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Once things settle down in Nod-Krai, I'd like to explore the world beyond Snezhnaya.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: You've told me so many stories about the other places you've been to, and all the friends you've made there... I'm curious to visit those nations and see them for myself.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It would also help me learn more about the journey that has made you into the person you are today.

choices.text: That's all the questions I have for now...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Okay. As you continue on your journey, don't forget to gaze up at the moon once in a while. It is, after all, no longer an illusion.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It shall cast down its true moonlight, connecting us in truth.

talks.objective: Write a letter to the Knights of Favonius

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "To Jean, Acting Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ugh, this preamble is such a pain to write. It's probably high time we got rid of this "Acting" business, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "I trust that Durin has updated you all on recent events. Hope we didn't worry you too much!"

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "The good news is, we managed to come together and put a stop to The Doctor's evil schemes. With that, I think it's safe to say that Nod-Krai is finally out of the woods."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "As for the Fatui — not counting The Damselette (aka, the Moon Goddess), who has left their organization —"

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "We found ourselves allied in this instance with both The Knave and Marionette (may she rest in peace)."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "As ever, we find ourselves better off for making friends rather than enemies. But until we can ascertain the Tsaritsa's true intentions, the future remains uncertain."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "In a short while..."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Wait, how am I meant to surprise everyone if I tell them in the letter that I'm heading home? That would be a huge waste.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Umm... Okay, got it!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "I will begin sending the expeditionary team back home in waves. I'm sure they'll be able to answer any questions you still have."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "I hope they won't gloss over the details of my many heroic deeds (but if they do, I'm sure it'll be because they're just too exhausted from the long journey)."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "I think of Mondstadt daily. Please give everyone my best regards."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #"P.S.: The Honorary Knight went above and beyond this time. Are there any other honors we can give {M#him}{F#her}? I'll leave it with you."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "P.P.S.: Please be extra nice to Klee for the foreseeable future. I cashed in on the last favor that the Hexenzirkel owed us, so we need to earn some more goodwill. If there's any serious problems, feel free to stick me in solitary confinement when I get back. I'll do the time for her."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Phew... And that, as they say, is all she wrote. End of an era!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And with the moon shining down brighter than ever, I think everyone is gonna sleep well tonight!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should probably head back...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: We're here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Over there.
